# Supertonic 3 reference fixtures

- `corpus.yaml`: eight ordinary English/Korean speech inputs using voices M1/F1,
  six real-inference latent-boundary probes, and five explicit rejection cases.
  The sentences are original MLSR test material under Apache-2.0.
- `frontend.yaml`: positive normalization/token expectations generated by the
  pinned upstream `UnicodeProcessor`, independently of MLSR's Python adaptation.
  Its provenance includes the source and Unicode-indexer hashes. Negative cases
  express MLSR's stricter validation policy.
- `reference-summary.yaml`: a compact record of the actual Core ML capture and
  replay, including device/software, model/corpus/tool hashes, shape routing,
  frame counts, and saved-noise/PCM hashes.
- `runtime-summary.yaml`: qualification of the persistent Rust runtime against
  those saved tensors, including ordinary allocation and alternating output
  buffers. This supplies frontend inputs and duration/bucket decisions from
  fixtures; it does not qualify the future Rust text-to-PCM pipeline.
- `planning.yaml`: raw duration, speed, and resulting duration Float32 bits plus
  frame/latent/bucket decisions extracted from the saved capture. This tests
  Rust's planning arithmetic on every real case without executing Core ML.
- `synthesis-summary.yaml`: complete Rust text-to-PCM qualification with saved
  noise, both allocation modes, input rejections, seeded normal/diagnostic
  comparisons, and standalone CLI WAV receipts. Runtime and synthesis records
  retain their own source hashes; the earlier runtime record is historical.
- `jobs-summary.yaml`: bounded paragraph jobs, cancellation and lifetime tests,
  including a real model run and repeated full-pipeline parity.
- `bindings-summary.yaml`: C static/shared and installed Python/Go/Dart synthesis,
  cancellation, independent audio ownership, cross-language PCM equality and
  cancel-then-WAV examples executed outside the repository checkout.

The six boundary probes target true latent lengths 127/128/129 and 255/256/257.
The harness predicts duration, then calibrates speaking rate to the middle of
the requested latent-length interval. Each effective rate is recorded and reused
unchanged during replay. These probes test routing and shape handling; they are
not naturalness evaluations at those rates.

Full captures live in an explicitly selected external directory. Each contains:

| File | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `reference.yaml` | Model/corpus identity, original and normalized text, requests, environment, checksums, and tensor inventory |
| `<case>.npz` | Named, non-pickled NumPy tensors, including actual initial noise, tokens/masks, styles, duration, text embedding, all eight VE states, true-length vocoder input, full waveform, and final PCM |
| `<case>.wav` | Exact final Float32 mono PCM in an IEEE-float WAV container at 44,100 Hz |

NPZ tensor hashes cover contiguous C-order tensor bytes; dtype and shape are
recorded separately. Exported tensor dtypes are little-endian int32/float32 on
the Apple Silicon capture host. PCM length is a frame count, not a byte count.
The final PCM is a prefix of the waveform determined by Float32 duration math.
Language tags count toward the 128-token text limit. Text is never truncated.

Replay reads `initial_noise` from the capture; it never regenerates noise from
the seed. This lets a later Rust or QNN implementation consume identical inputs
without reproducing NumPy's random-number generator. Integer tensors must match
exactly. Float comparisons have explicit absolute/relative tolerances, with
bit-exactness reported separately. OS/runtime changes may change floating-point
outputs; preserve the original evidence and investigate rather than silently
refreshing expectations.

The reference is the pinned **Core ML baseline**, not a claim of exact equality
to the original unquantized ONNX model. CPU+ANE is an execution policy, not proof
of all-ANE placement. Capture/replay does not establish perceptual quality,
intelligibility across the full model language set, or runtime performance.

Commands and storage rules are in the [tool README](../../../tools/supertonic3/README.md).
